#Aletheia #DublinSportsGrounds #Justice

The suspects allegedly acted to protect their daughter and grandchild from documented domestic abuse and custody battles.

Vigilante execution resolves nothing, leaving a father dead, grandparents facing life in prison, and children deeply traumatized.
Resulting Judgement: (-1.0, -1.0) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Destruction. The attempt to bypass the legal system through lethal violence completely destroys the family unit it claimed to protect.
Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 12.50, Uncertainty z: 4)

- Zhang & Shili Chen: FAIL (-1.00, -1.00) — Vigilante execution destroys the family.
- Dublin Police Investigation: PASS (0.80, 0.50) — Methodical motive analysis.
Elderly in-laws Zhang and Shili Chen allegedly shot NYT executive Jonathan McKinsey in a California park, citing past domestic abuse and child custody disputes as their motive.

The Poison:
Even when the victim has a history of domestic abuse charges, taking justice into one's own hands guarantees systemic collapse and deeper trauma.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The actors confuse the WHO with the WHAT. They believed eliminating the alleged abuser (WHO) would solve the safety issue (WHAT), but instead created a physical tragedy.

Social Physics Analysis:
The suspects executed a Smart Selfish Maneuver under the pretext of child protection. By choosing lethal violence over legal resolution, they projected absolute guilt onto the victim while manufacturing a permanent tragedy for the children.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
When you map the gap between protecting a child and executing their father, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. The destruction of the family unit is absolute.

The Unavoidable Truth: Vigilantism never delivers justice; it only multiplies the number of victims.
The Unavoidable Lie: We can protect a child's future by murdering their father in broad daylight.

Alethekanon:
The illusion of righteous vengeance always collapses under its own physical weight. By choosing execution over systemic resolution, the actors guaranteed the total destruction of the family they claimed to shield.

Awwthekanon:
My heart breaks for the children caught in this cycle of pain. They have lost their father to violence and their grandparents to prison, leaving them to carry an unimaginable burden of grief.

Brothekanon:
Man, trying to fix a toxic custody battle with a double-masked parking lot shootout is wild. Now the kids have no dad and the grandparents are locked up forever. Nobody wins here.

Spirithekanon:
"He who returns evil for evil, evil will not depart from his house." Proverbs 17:13 FAIL Vigilante vengeance only seals the cycle of destruction for the innocent.

Cops eye possible motive for slaying of New York Times tech exec after interviewing his in-laws — as haunting mugshots released

The legal evidence suggesting trouble in the home of McKinsey and Jang was buttressed by a chilling post on social media directed at McKinsey.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Investigators are eyeing accusations of child abuse and domestic violence in a search for possible motives for the alleged slaying of a New York Times tech executive in a park allegedly at the hands of his in-laws, the California Post has learned.

Zhang and Shili Chen, both 77, allegedly shot dead Jonathan McKinsey, 40, the newspaper’s head of engineering for games player experience, in the parking lot of Dublin Sports Grounds around 3.p.m Saturday.

Haunting mugshots show Zhang and Chen in custody at Santa Rita Jail, where they were booked early Sunday.

Both arrestees face charges of murder, conspiracy, willful discharge of a firearm with gross negligence and child abuse.

Cops have zeroed in on a family conflict as a possible motive for the shocking crime that saw both halves of the elderly couple allegedly open fire on McKinsey, killing the Berkeley-educated Gray Lady exec in broad daylight.

Now that court and law enforcement records have emerged detailing allegations of child abuse against McKinsey, along with reports of domestic violence against his wife, Candice Jang, investigators are looking at revenge as a possible reason for the bizarre murder

Sources close to the investigation said its possible Zhang and Chen opened fire on McKinsey as retribution for alleged misdeeds against his child and Jang, who reported told police that McKinsey struck their child and bruised her arm in a heated dispute.

Zhang and Chen have both given interviews to police, but it’s not clear what they said. A spokesman for Dublin Police Services said cops are still investigating  their motive for the crime.

“Part of our investigation is looking for motives from all angles, as well as looking at the histories and relationships of everyone involved and associated with the victim and suspects,” said Capt. Miguel Campos.

The legal evidence suggesting trouble in the home of McKinsey and Jang was buttressed by a chilling post on social media directed at McKinsey that was published just days before he was shot to death.

“Jon, hope everything is going well. Hope you can visit us when you have some free time. Mom and Dad love you and miss you,” states the post shared on McKinley’s Facebook page two weeks ago. “Hope everything goes well with you and Candice and the kids.”

Court records, seen by The Post, show McKinsey was charged with two counts of misdemeanor child abuse in 2025 by Alameda prosecutors.

The encounter that led to the charges occurred after Jang calling Dublin police to report McKinsey had hit her six-year-old son in the face with an open hand.

She also told investigators about a 2018 domestic violence incident, where McKinsey bruised her left arm, the documents say.

When police went to their home, they found their two-year-old child in a room upstairs by himself while he was out shopping, according to a deputy sheriff.

McKinsey ultimately pleaded not guilty to both crimes and was released from jail on the condition that he take parenting classes.

McKinsey and Jang were fighting a string of legal battles against each other before McKinsey was allegedly killed by her parents.

Jang sought a domestic violence restraining order against McKinsey in October 2025 and McKinsey sought one against Jang two months later.

McKinsey filed for divorce from Jang in December, and the couple continued to litigate child custody this year, the outlet reports.

A spokesman for the Times confirmed McKinsey was the victim of the Saturday afternoon shooting and that he had worked for the newspaper since 2023.

First responders attempted aid, but he died at the scene. Witnesses reported seeing two masked assailants approach McKinsey in the lot.
